findings.reason: the fix is confined to what the refresh child records and stores, so the overstatement changes no node's work, and the wrong-grain argument against §19's revision identity stands regardless.
findings.text: "The served process never runs those derivations itself, so its stale-code check (reckon/served_code.py) never sees them change" is contradicted by the served read path: _served_result (reckon/route_results.py:422) derives a cold miss inline through _route_compute → _compute_refresh, and it is called from the served handlers for the rollup (reckon/serve.py:2945), the checks summary (reckon/serve.py:3258) and discovery (reckon/serve.py:3317), so those definitions do enter the served process's ExecutedSource on a cold miss. The incident is explained by the warm case (a stored result meant no in-process derivation ran), not by a structural impossibility

findings.reason: the section's own preceding sentence ("It stores the fingerprint of those definitions' source") states the definition-level mechanism, so a worker reading the whole deliverable resolves the tension toward fingerprints, and the done-when fails loudly if it does not.
findings.text: the cost clause allows a file-level revision check ("no more than a stat of the files those definitions live in, memoized by file revision"), but a definition the child did not run may live in a file whose revision moved because a different definition in it changed, and a file-level check would then retire the result and fail the section's own case "A rewrite of a definition the child did not run leaves the result served"; only re-fingerprinting the recorded definitions after a file moves satisfies that case

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — 4ebe2643a resolves to §20's merge; _compute_refresh (reckon/route_results.py:235), ExecutedSource (reckon/served_code.py:752), _fingerprint (reckon/served_code.py:325), _attach_schedule (reckon/serve.py:1746) and reckon/route_results.py:251 all resolve exactly as cited.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §21's done-when is measurable and carries a negative control, but its cost clause "Checking costs no more than a stat of the files those definitions live in" is narrower than the definition-level comparison its own case "A rewrite of a definition the child did not run leaves the result served" requires.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections place every log "under the run directory" ending in EXIT=, on the durable crew run path, not a scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags appear in either section's prose or in its new test filenames (tests/test_a_stored_result_follows_the_code_that_derived_it.py, tests/test_the_schedule_is_attached_when_it_is_read.py).
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §21's mechanism and its done-when are sound and its fix reaches the real code path (the child entry _compute_refresh and the read _refresh_result in reckon/route_results.py), but its stated root cause overstates: the served process does run the derivations itself on a cold miss, so the claim that its stale-code check "never sees them change" does not hold universally.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §21 carries one deliverable (a stored result's identity is the fingerprints of the definitions that derived it) and §22 carries one (the schedule is attached at read, not at store).
